m-04.title: Buy snacks with 5000원
m-04.goal: Find different ways wey meet several conditions together, explain how to find all without miss any, and why some cases impossible.
m-04.material: Our group of 10 people wan buy snacks for party. Chips cost 600원 per bag, jelly 400원 per bag, and drink 500원 per bottle. We spend exactly 5000원, buy at least one of all three, and get at least 10 items altogether so each person get one.
m-04.thinking.2: Explain impossible cases with even and odd numbers
m-04.prereq.0: Calculate money using multiplication and addition (Grade 3-4 level)
m-04.s.s1.prompt: Make three different purchase plans wey meet all conditions.
m-04.s.s1.hint.0: First choose how many of one kind to buy, then check if you fit buy other two kinds with remaining money.
m-04.s.s1.hint.1: If total below or above 5000원, change number of one kind one by one to fix difference.
m-04.s.s1.fail.c1: You gats buy at least one of every kind.
m-04.s.s1.fail.c3: Total no be 5000원. Add amount for each kind to check.
m-04.s.s1.fail.c4: Items fewer than 10, so no be enough for everybody.
m-04.s.s2.prompt: After you find one way, how best to find other ways without miss any?
m-04.s.s2.hint.0: Put ways you find in table and check the order you find dem.
m-04.s.s2.hint.1: For each option, compare "how far you search after finding one" and "whether you fit know you find all."
m-04.s.s2.o.a: Set chip bags as 1,2,3... in order, and stop as soon as one way work 1 2
m-04.s.s2.r.a: Going in order good. But if you stop after one, you no know if more ways dey. You gats go far enough to find all without missing any.
m-04.s.s2.o.b: Try calculations as dem come mind, keep only those that total 5000원, stop when no more appear
m-04.s.s2.r.b: You fit find some ways, but you no fit know if you "find dem all." To get all without miss any, you need order.
m-04.s.s2.o.c: Set drink bottles as 1,2,3... all the way in order, and for each, check if remaining money fit buy rest. 1 2
m-04.s.s2.r.c: Good method. Fix one kind in order all the way and check other things; you know how far you reach, so you fit find all without miss any.
m-04.s.s2.o.d: When total pass 5000원, reduce all three kinds by one each and calculate again, then repeat
m-04.s.s2.r.d: Three kinds get different prices, so reducing all equally no fix difference. Easier to adjust one kind at a time.
m-04.s.s2.explain: If you fix one kind in order and check others all the way, you know how far you reach, so you fit find all without miss any. For example, check drinks at 1 bottle, 2 bottles, 3 bottles, and so on.
m-04.s.s3.prompt: Challenge (optional): For ways you find, drink bottle count (500원) na 2,4,6, or 8, always even. No way buy odd number bottles (1,3,5...)? Explain why with your own words. Even/odd, 200원 units, or table all useful. 1 2 3 4
m-04.s.s3.hint.0: Turn 600원, 400원, and 500원 into 100원 bundles, write dem as 6, 4, 5.
m-04.s.s3.hint.1: Find money wey remain if you buy 1 bottle and 3 bottles drinks, check if chips and jelly fit make that amount.
m-04.s.s3.placeholder: For example: Chips and jelly cost ... If drink bottle number odd, ...
m-04.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You write wetin special about amount you get by adding chips and jelly prices?
m-04.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You continue and explain why total no fit be 5000원 when drink bottle count odd?
m-04.s.s3.model.0: If you count 600원 and 400원 in 100원 bundles, you get 6 bundles and 4 bundles, both even. 5000원 na 50 bundles, even too. Drink cost 5 bundles, so with odd bottle count total go be odd and no fit equal 50, wey even.
m-04.s.s3.model.1: Chips at 600 won and jelly at 400 won both be multiples of 200 won, so their sum too be multiple of 200. Odd number of drink bottles cost 500, 1500, 2500..., and if you divide dem by 200, remainder na 100. So you no fit add am to make 5000 won.
m-04.s.s3.model.2: With 1 drink bottle, money wey remain na 4500 won, but any amount made with 600 and 400 won na multiple of 200, so 4500 no fit make. With 3 or 5 bottles, remaining amount no be multiple of 200 too, so e no work.

m-02.title: Wetin else we need to solve this problem?
m-02.goal: Learn say whether problem fit solve depend no be on whether numbers dey there, but whether we get info needed for wetin question ask; point out exactly which info missing and explain why division with remainder gats round up.
m-02.material:
Students wey dey go field trip wan share into vans. Four problems dey below.
a) 28 students share and ride in vans. One van fit carry at most 9 students. Wetin be least number of vans we need?
b) 28 students dey go field trip. Entry fee na 2000원 per student, and van rental na 90000원 per van. Wetin be total entry fee for all students?
c) Students share and ride in vans. One van fit carry at most 9 students. Wetin be least number of vans we need?
d) 28 students dey go field trip. One van fit carry at most 9 students. How much e go cost altogether to rent vans?
m-02.thinking.2: Make different values wey fit the conditions
m-02.prereq.0: Quotient and remainder in division (Grade 3-4 level)
m-02.s.s1.prompt: Read each problem one by one and choose all wey fit answer using only information inside am.
m-02.s.s1.hint.0: For each of four problems, underline wetin dem ask you to find.
m-02.s.s1.hint.1: Write the numbers you need to calculate the answer, then check if each one dey in problem. Mark numbers wey you no use.
m-02.s.s1.r.a: If you miss problem a): e get both 28 students and capacity of 9 for each van, so e fit solve.
m-02.s.s1.r.b: If you miss problem b): even though extra info like rental fee dey inside but you no use am, you fit find "total entry fee" with 28×2000. Extra information different from missing information.
m-02.s.s1.r.c: If you choose problem c): even though numbers dey, some info wey you really need to find answer no dey. Check which numbers you need to work out wetin question ask.
m-02.s.s1.r.d: If you choose problem d): you fit find number of vans (4), but to find cost you need rental fee for one van. That number no dey in problem.
m-02.s.s1.explain: Problem a) fit solve because e include 28 students and capacity 9 per van. Problem b) no use rental fee, but "entry fee × number of students" (2000×28=56000원) answer am. Problem c) no say how many students dey, and problem d) no give rental fee for one van, so no fit solve dem. Problem fit solve with extra info wey no needed, but if needed info missing, many numbers no go help.
m-02.s.s2.prompt: Wetin you suppose ask teacher wey write problem so you fit solve problem c)?
m-02.s.s2.hint.0: Compare numbers in problem c) and problem a) side by side.
m-02.s.s2.hint.1: Find information wey dey in a) but no dey in c).
m-02.s.s2.r.a: Good question. Number of students na info we really need to find number of vans, but problem no include am.
m-02.s.s2.r.b: How many vans needed na wetin question ask. Asking for answer no give new information.
m-02.s.s2.o.c: How many students fit ride inside one van?
m-02.s.s2.r.c: That information already dey in problem c). Read again and find missing info.
m-02.s.s2.o.d: How much rental fee per van?
m-02.s.s2.r.d: Rental fee only useful after you know how many vans. E no help find how many vans needed.
m-02.s.s2.explain: Problem c) get capacity per van but no total student count. You need both total students and capacity to find "how many vans."
m-02.s.s3.prompt: Choose number of students so exactly 3 vans needed, then find 3 different student counts wey work. (Capacity per van na 9.)
m-02.s.s3.hint.0: Find most people 2 vans fit carry and most people 3 vans fit carry.
m-02.s.s3.hint.1: Choose number of students and count by hand how many vans fit carry dem.
m-02.s.s3.fail.c1: Use whole number 1 or more for number of students.
m-02.s.s3.fail.c2: With this student count, number of vans no be 3. Check max 3 vans fit carry and whether 2 vans enough.
m-02.s.s3.explain: 2 vans fit carry up to 18 students, 3 vans up to 27. So if students from 19 through 27 (9 possible numbers), exactly 3 vans needed.
m-02.s.s4.prompt: With 27 students, you need 3 vans; with 28 you need 4. 28÷9=3.11…, so why 4 vans, no be 3?
m-02.s.s4.hint.0: First write how many students fit ride if all 3 vans full.
m-02.s.s4.hint.1: Then compare with 28 students and check if any person remain.
m-02.s.s4.selfAssess.0: Your explanation include max number of people 3 vans fit carry?
m-02.s.s4.selfAssess.1: You say student wey remain still gats ride inside van?
m-02.s.s4.model.0: 3 vans fit carry only 27, so 1 student remain. That 1 still need ride, so another van needed, making 4 vans.
m-02.s.s4.model.1: If 28 students enter 3 vans, only 27 fit go; 1 no fit. So you need 4 vans. You no fit just drop decimal part.
m-02.s.s4.model.2: 3 vans no fit carry all 28 students. Even if full, dem carry 27, one student remain, so we need another van.
m-02.s.s4.model.3: 28 divided by 9 na 3 remainder 1, but the remaining student still need ride, so we need one more van.

m-11.title: Wetin we need know to determine a quadratic function?
m-11.goal: Judge which info sets uniquely determine quadratic function; where info too little, make two different functions meeting condition and decide extra info needed.
m-11.material: You wan find equation of quadratic function f(x)=ax²+bx+c (a≠0). From info sets below, find those where information alone uniquely determine equation.
m-11.thinking.1: Show information no enough with two different examples
m-11.prereq.0: Three forms of quadratic function (standard form, vertex form, factored form)
m-11.prereq.2: Put points wey graph pass through inside
m-11.s.s1.prompt: Choose every info set wey by itself uniquely determine quadratic function.
m-11.s.s1.hint.0: For f(x)=ax²+bx+c, first count how many unknowns to find.
m-11.s.s1.hint.1: Check how many different equations (conditions) each option give, and if dem determine a,b,c all.
m-11.s.s1.o.a: Vertex and one point on graph wey no be vertex
m-11.s.s1.r.a: If e be vertex, p and q set inside f(x)=a(x−p)²+q, and one point set a.
m-11.s.s1.o.b: Two different points on graph, and graph opens upward
m-11.s.s1.r.b: Infinitely many upward-opening parabolas pass through two points. Opening direction only tell sign of a, not a value.
m-11.s.s1.o.c: Two x-intercepts and x-coordinate of vertex
m-11.s.s1.r.c: Di x-coordinate wey vertex dey exactly halfway between di two x-intercepts, so e no be new information. a still remain. Try multiply (x−1)(x−3) by 2 or −5.
m-11.s.s1.o.d: Three points for di graph wey get different x-coordinates
m-11.s.s1.r.d: Three points dey give three independent equations for a, b, and c, so dem fit determine am one way only.
m-11.s.s1.o.e: Di equation for axis of symmetry and di y-intercept
m-11.s.s1.r.e: Di axis of symmetry dey set one relationship between a and b, and di y-intercept dey set c. Count whether dem don determine all three values a, b, and c.
m-11.s.s1.o.f: Two points wey e meet di x-axis, plus one other point for di graph
m-11.s.s1.r.f: For f(x)=a(x−p)(x−q), dem don determine p and q, and one point dey determine a.
m-11.s.s1.explain: Three things no dey known, a, b, and c, so you need three independent conditions. D: three points dey give three simultaneous equations. A: di vertex dey determine p and q for f(x)=a(x−p)²+q, and one point dey determine a. F: dem don determine p and q for f(x)=a(x−p)(x−q), and one point dey determine a. B, C, and E get only two independent conditions, so a still remain. (If three points dey one straight line, quadratic function no dey, so since di condition be say na quadratic function, di three points no dey one straight line.)
m-11.s.s2.prompt: You wan show say di information for option E, "di y-intercept na 1 and di axis of symmetry na x=2," no dey determine di equation by itself. Make two different quadratic functions f(x)=ax²+bx+c wey meet both conditions.
m-11.s.s2.hint.0: Di axis of symmetry na x=−b/(2a), so write di relationship between a and b wey go make am equal 2.
m-11.s.s2.hint.1: Choose a first, then fit b and c to di conditions. Check say di conditions still dey true when you change a.
m-11.s.s2.ok.c1: Since a no be 0, na quadratic function.
m-11.s.s2.fail.c1: a no suppose be 0 for am to be quadratic function.
m-11.s.s2.ok.c2: Di y-intercept (di value when x=0) na 1.
m-11.s.s2.fail.c2: Di y-intercept na di value wey you get when you put x=0, f(0)=c. Dis no be 1.
m-11.s.s2.ok.c3: Di axis of symmetry na x=2.
m-11.s.s2.fail.c3: Di axis of symmetry na x=−b/(2a). Check whether dis value na 2.
m-11.s.s2.explain: If di axis of symmetry na x=2, den −b/(2a)=2, so b=−4a; and if di y-intercept na 1, den c=1. So a fit be any value wey no be 0. For example, x²−4x+1 and 2x²−8x+1 both meet di conditions. Since a dey free, dem no determine di equation.
m-11.s.s3.prompt: You wan get one more information to add to "di y-intercept na 1 and di axis of symmetry na x=2" (option E), so dem go determine di equation one way only. Wetin you go ask di person wey write di question? Write di question and, for one or two sentences, explain why dat information dey determine di equation.
m-11.s.s3.hint.0: Write which of a, b, and c option E don already determine, and which one you still no know.
m-11.s.s3.hint.1: Think about di information wey you fit put inside di equation to determine a.
m-11.s.s3.placeholder: Example: One other point wey di graph pass through ...
m-11.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Di information wey you choose dey determine di remaining unknown (a) one way only?
m-11.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Na information wey no overlap with di information wey you already get (di y-intercept and di axis of symmetry)?
m-11.s.s3.model.0: Ask for one point wey di graph pass through, wey no dey x=0 or x=4. Di points for x=0 and x=4 na di same as wetin you already know, so dem no be new information. If you put one other point inside di equation, e go determine a one way only.
m-11.s.s3.model.1: Ask wetin di minimum (or maximum) value be. Di value for di axis of symmetry x=2 na di minimum, so dem don determine f(2)=1−4a and you fit find a.
m-11.s.s3.model.2: Ask for di coefficient a of x². Dem don already determine b and c, so if you know a, dem go determine di equation one way only.

m-03.title: Guess wetin dey inside marble bag
m-03.goal: Change your first guess as more data come in, and explain why small number of draws no enough to be certain.
m-03.material: One bag wey you no fit see inside get 10 marbles altogether, red and blue. You draw one, check color, put am back, and repeat many times. You no know how many marbles of each color dey.
m-03.thinking.0: Change judgment when new data show
m-03.thinking.1: Connect amount of data with how sure you be
m-03.thinking.2: Join the results to choose most reasonable explanation
m-03.prereq.0: Write part of whole as fraction or percent (Grade 5-6 level)
m-03.prereq.1: Count and organize counts in table
m-03.s.s1.prompt: Data dey reveal bit by bit. At each step choose your idea about wetin dey inside bag.
m-03.s.s1.hint.0: At every step, divide number of red draws by total draws to find ratio.
m-03.s.s1.hint.1: For each option, divide red marble count by 10 (share of red in bag) and compare with ratio from your draws.
m-03.s.s1.st.0.info: You draw 5 times: red 4 times, blue 1 time.
m-03.s.s1.st.0.ask: Which color you think more plenty inside bag?
m-03.s.s1.st.0.after: Five draws small, so clue dey but no certainty yet. E reasonable to say red fit more.
m-03.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Red show 4 times out of 5, so blue go come next to balance am; blue go be more
m-03.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Marble go back inside bag, so earlier color no change next draw. No think in "turns"; check how many times each color show.
m-03.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Red show 4 times, so red must plenty; no need draw again
m-03.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Five draws small. One color fit show often just by chance.
m-03.s.s1.st.0.o.c: Red fit be more, but 5 draws small and chance fit cause am, so make we draw more
m-03.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Good judgment. You consider both things: clue dey, but draws too few to be certain.
m-03.s.s1.st.0.o.d: Five draws no tell us anything about which color more, so result useless
m-03.s.s1.st.0.r.d: E no certain, but clue dey. Red showing more na information too.
m-03.s.s1.st.1.info: You increase to 20 draws and got red 9 times, blue 11 times.
m-03.s.s1.st.1.after: With red 9 and blue 11 out of 20, difference no big. E right to change first guess and think dem about equal.
m-03.s.s1.st.1.o.a: Red and blue show about same for 20 draws, so still hard to decide which one more
m-03.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You judge using new data too. You adjust first guess to match data.
m-03.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Red show more in first 5 draws, so I think red more, no matter wetin 20 draws show
m-03.s.s1.st.1.r.b: You hold on only to first 5 draws. What if you consider am together with new data?
m-03.s.s1.st.1.o.c: Blue show 2 more times for 20 draws, so I sure say blue plenty more
m-03.s.s1.st.1.r.c: 9 and 11 close. Too early to say "plenty more" for sure.
m-03.s.s1.st.2.info: You increase to 50 draws and got red 19 times, blue 31 times.
m-03.s.s1.st.2.ask: Choose marble count wey best fit ratio of red draws (19/50).
m-03.s.s1.st.2.after: Red-draw ratio 19/50 na 0.38, closest to 0.4, the ratio for 4 marbles among options. 5 marbles (0.5) no impossible, but e fit less well than 4. More data make your guess narrower.
m-03.s.s1.st.2.r.a: If red na 8, red suppose show about 40 times from 50 draws. But e show only 19 times.
m-03.s.s1.st.2.r.b: If na 5, red ratio suppose be about 0.5, but actual 19/50=0.38 lower. 5 no impossible, but no be "best fit."
m-03.s.s1.st.2.r.c: 19/50=0.38 closest to 0.4, ratio for 4 marbles. You compare ratios and choose best fit.
m-03.s.s1.st.2.r.d: When data change, likelihood of each option change too. Compare 19/50 with ratio for each case.
m-03.s.s1.reflect: How first 5 draws differ from 50 draws, and how your mind change? How your "certainty" gats differ when data small and when data plenty?
m-03.s.s2.prompt: Wetin you wan tell friend wey shout "Red plenty!" after first 5 draws only?
m-03.s.s2.hint.0: Think which result you trust more, 5 draws or 50, and explain why.
m-03.s.s2.hint.1: End by suggesting wetin your friend fit try next.
m-03.s.s2.selfAssess.0: You say "data small" or "make we draw more"?
m-03.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You use the 20 or 50 draw results you see as reason?
m-03.s.s2.model.0: Five draws fit just be chance, so make we draw more. When we do 20 and 50 draws, blue come out more.
m-03.s.s2.model.1: Draws too few, so we never sure. We need do more.
m-03.s.s2.model.2: The sample small, so we no suppose sure about result. If we repeat more times, e become more reliable.

m-07.s.s2.fail.c1: Scores must at least 0 and at most 100.
m-07.title: If two classes get same average, dem equally good?
m-07.goal: Use data you make yourself show spread fit differ even with same average, then set question for friend to solve.
m-07.material: Three students picked from Class 1 and Class 2 each, and math scores checked. Average for both classes na 70 points. Teacher say, "Since averages same, scores in both classes similar." (Students picked imaginary.)
m-07.thinking.0: Judge limit of comparing with average alone
m-07.thinking.1: Make your own data meeting conditions
m-07.thinking.2: Make question whose answer depend on data
m-07.s.s1.prompt: Which thought about teacher statement most appropriate?
m-07.s.s1.hint.0: Think of one set of 3 scores wey average na 70.
m-07.s.s1.hint.1: Make 2 different sets of 3 scores with mean 70 and compare dem.
m-07.s.s1.o.a: If average same, scores generally go gather to similar degree
m-07.s.s1.r.a: Average pack values into one number, so e no tell whether scores gather or spread. Compare case where all 3 same with case where dem far apart.
m-07.s.s1.o.b: Even if averages same, score spread fit different for the two classes
m-07.s.s1.r.b: You point out say even with same average, scores fit gather or spread far apart.
m-07.s.s1.o.c: If averages same, highest scores generally too similar
m-07.s.s1.r.c: Even with same average, one class fit get similar scores, while other get mix of high and low. You no fit say top scores same.
m-07.s.s1.explain: Even with same mean, scores fit gather like 70, 70, 70 or spread like 40, 70, 100. Make dem and check next step.
m-07.s.s2.prompt: Make scores (whole numbers from 0 to 100) for two classes. Conditions: each class mean 70, and Class 2 (highest score−lowest score) must be at least 20 points bigger than Class 1's. Changing score order alone count as same example, so make 2 different score combinations.
m-07.s.s2.hint.0: First choose 3 scores for Class 1 wey add to 210, and calculate highest minus lowest.
m-07.s.s2.hint.1: For Class 2, keep total 210 and try raise one score, lower another to make difference bigger.
m-07.s.s2.fail.c3: Class 1 three scores no add to 210. Sum must be 210 for average 70.
m-07.s.s2.ok.c5: Class 2 get spread at least 20 points bigger than Class 1.
m-07.s.s2.fail.c5: Class 2 (highest−lowest) no be at least 20 points bigger than Class 1. Calculate each class difference and compare.
m-07.s.s2.explain: Both classes get average 70 points, but for (70, 70, 70) the difference na 0 points, and for (40, 70, 100) e na 60 points. Even with same average, scores fit spread different.
m-07.s.s3.prompt: Using two classes scores you just make, write one question friend fit answer and provide answer too. (Example: "Which class get higher ○○?")
m-07.s.s3.hint.0: Choose one different value from highest score, lowest score, and range, and turn am into question.
m-07.s.s3.hint.1: After writing question, look at scores and answer am. Check say answer only one.
m-07.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Answer depend only on scores of two classes you make?
m-07.s.s3.selfAssess.1: This question no fit answer just from fact say "averages same"?
m-07.s.s3.selfAssess.2: Another friend go get the same answer using your data?
m-07.s.s3.model.0: Question: Between Class 1 (70, 70, 70) and Class 2 (40, 70, 100), which class scores gather more evenly? Answer: Class 1. Difference between highest and lowest na 0, wey smaller than Class 2 difference of 60.
m-07.s.s3.model.1: Question: Both classes average 70 points, so which class get higher top score? Answer: Class 2 (100 points). Even with same average, top score fit different.

m-06.title: Checking Seoyeon solution
m-06.goal: Learn say dividing both sides of equation by expression with variable fit lose a solution if you forget that it might be 0; correct solution and make equation where same thing happen.
m-06.material: Seoyeon solve equation x² (x squared) = 3x this way. Read solution one line at a time and check whether e correct.
m-06.thinking.0: Find where and why solution get mistake
m-06.thinking.2: Make a case where same mistake happen
m-06.prereq.0: Solve quadratic equations by factoring (Grade 9 level)
m-06.prereq.1: Check equation solution by putting am back in
m-06.s.s1.prompt: Choose one line in solution wey you no fit trust. (You fit choose wrong step or wrong conclusion caused by mistake.)
m-06.s.s1.hint.0: Check one line at a time whether each line follow properly from line just before am.
m-06.s.s1.hint.1: Try put x=0 inside original equation x²=3x and check whether e hold.
m-06.s.s1.line.1: Divide both sides by x to get x=3
m-06.s.s1.line.2: Putting x=3 give 3²=9 and 3×3=9, so e hold.
m-06.s.s1.line.3: So only solution to this equation na x=3.
m-06.s.s1.explain: Wetin you see depend on which line you choose. If you choose line 3 (substitution), calculation correct. But substitution only show "3 na one solution"; e no show "no other solutions dey." If you choose line 1, na original equation, no problem. Wrong lines na 2 and 4. For line 2 dem divide both sides by x, but x fit be 0, and you no fit divide by 0. So solution x=0 disappear, leading to wrong conclusion for line 4: "only solution na 3."
m-06.s.s2.prompt: Find all solutions for x²=3x correctly, and explain where Seoyeon solution go wrong.
m-06.s.s2.hint.0: Write what expression you get when you move all terms to one side and factor.
m-06.s.s2.hint.1: Put Seoyeon solution and yours side by side, and find where dem start to differ.
m-06.s.s2.placeholder: Example: If I move terms and simplify, ...
m-06.s.s2.selfAssess.0: You check by putting x=0 and x=3 into original equation?

m-12.title: Looking at one question about arithmetic sequence
m-12.goal: Discover say for arithmetic sequence, terms wey their index numbers add up to di same sum get di same sum of terms. So dem fit solve question wey look like e no get enough information, and you fit make your own question wey use dis property.
m-12.material: One question dey: for arithmetic sequence {aₙ}, if a₃ + a₇ = 20, find a₅. Suyoung talk say, "We no know di first term or di common difference, so we no fit solve am." (Make di first term be a and di common difference be d. a₃ mean di 3rd term, a₇ di 7th term, and a₅ di 5th term.)
m-12.thinking.0: Finding one value wey no dey change across plenty cases
m-12.thinking.1: Judge again whether di information plenty
m-12.thinking.2: Making question wey use one property
m-12.prereq.0: General term for arithmetic sequence aₙ=a+(n−1)d
m-12.s.s1.prompt: Make three arithmetic sequences wey their first terms a and common differences d different, and wey satisfy a₃+a₇=20.
m-12.s.s1.hint.0: Write a₃ and a₇ using a and d, and write di equation wey you get when you add dem.
m-12.s.s1.hint.1: Choose d first and find a from dat equation.
m-12.s.s1.fail.c1: a₃+a₇ no be 20. Add a₃=a+2d and a₇=a+6d make you check am.
m-12.s.s1.explain: a₃+a₇=2a+8d=20, so a=10−4d. When d na 0, 1, 2, −1, di first terms na 10, 6, 2, 14.
m-12.s.s2.prompt: Find di 5th term a₅ for each sequence wey you just make. Wetin you notice?
m-12.s.s2.hint.0: Really calculate a₅ for each sequence wey you just make. (How many times you add di common difference to di first term to get a₅?)
m-12.s.s2.hint.1: Put di a₅ values wey you calculate side by side and compare dem.
m-12.s.s2.o.a: a₅ dey different for each sequence, so dis information alone no fit determine a₅
m-12.s.s2.r.a: Check di values wey you calculate again. Think about how many times dem add di common difference to di first term to get a₅.
m-12.s.s2.o.b: a₅ na di same value for every sequence, so dis information alone dey determine a₅
m-12.s.s2.r.b: Even though di first term and common difference different for each sequence, a₅ na di same for all of dem. Dem fit solve am even though di information look like e no plenty.
m-12.s.s2.o.c: Di bigger di common difference, di bigger a₅, so you need to know di common difference to determine a₅
m-12.s.s2.r.c: Really calculate a₅ when di common difference na 0, 1, and 2, and check whether e change. Notice say di first term change too.
m-12.s.s2.o.d: Di bigger di first term, di bigger a₅, so you need to know di first term to determine a₅
m-12.s.s2.r.d: Really calculate a₅ when di first term na 10, 6, and 2. Di common difference change too.
m-12.s.s2.explain: For (10,0), a₅=10; for (6,1), 6+4=10; for (2,2), 2+8=10; for (14,−1), 14−4=10, so e na 10 every time. a₅ na di first term plus di common difference 4 times (a+4d), and from a₃+a₇=2a+8d=20, we get a+4d=10. Contrary to wetin Suyoung talk, dem don determine a₅ even if you no know di first term and di common difference.
m-12.s.s3.prompt: Choose all di cases wey, if dem tell you di value of di sum of two terms aₘ+aₙ like a₃+a₇, you fit find a₅ without knowing di first term and di common difference. (You fit find out by testing di plenty sequences wey you make before.)
m-12.s.s3.hint.0: Write di expression for a₅ using a and d side by side with di expression for each option sum using a and d, then compare dem.
m-12.s.s3.hint.1: For any option wey di sum no equal 2 times a₅, make two sequences by yourself wey get di same sum but different a₅, then check.
m-12.s.s3.r.a: a₂+a₉=2a+9d. Di coefficient of d different from 2a+8d, wey na 2 times a₅, so you no fit determine a₅.
m-12.s.s3.r.b: If you miss a₁+a₉: e na 2a+8d, wey equal 2 times a₅.
m-12.s.s3.r.c: a₃+a₆=2a+7d get different coefficient of d from 2a+8d, wey na 2 times a₅. Check whether sequences dey wey get di same value but different a₅.
m-12.s.s3.r.d: a₆+a₈=2a+12d. Di coefficient of d different from 2a+8d, wey na 2 times a₅.
m-12.s.s3.r.e: If you miss a₄+a₆: e na 2a+8d, wey equal 2 times a₅.
m-12.s.s3.r.f: If you miss a₂+a₈: e na 2a+8d, wey equal 2 times a₅.
m-12.s.s3.explain: aₘ+aₙ=2a+(m+n−2)d and 2a₅=2a+8d, so di sum go equal 2a₅ only when m+n−2=8, dat is, m+n=10. a₄+a₆, a₁+a₉, and a₂+a₈ all get index sum of 10. Di other ones get different index sums, so di coefficient of d different and dem no determine a₅.
m-12.s.s4.prompt: Use dis property (if di index numbers add up to di same sum, di terms get di same sum) to make your own arithmetic sequence question wey answer fit determine even though di first term and common difference no dey known, then write di answer and solution in one or two sentences.
m-12.s.s4.hint.0: Choose di index of di term wey you wan find and compare am with di indexes of di two terms wey you go give. Remember wetin you find for s3.
m-12.s.s4.hint.1: Choose one first term and one common difference, calculate by hand for di question wey you make, and check say di answer correct.
m-12.s.s4.placeholder: Example: For arithmetic sequence {a_n}, ... (You fit type a₂ as a_2)

m-12.s.s4.selfAssess.1: You check di answer wey you write by choosing one first term and common difference and calculating by hand?
m-12.s.s4.selfAssess.2: Di solution make am clear say your friend fit solve am even without knowing di first term and di common difference?
m-12.s.s4.model.0: For arithmetic sequence {a_n}, if a_2 + a_10 = 36, find di value of a_6. Answer: 18. Since 2+10=12=6+6, a_2+a_10=2a_6.
m-12.s.s4.model.1: For arithmetic sequence {a_n}, if a_1 + a_11 = 40, wetin be di value of a_6? Di answer na 20. Di index sum 1+11=12=6+6, so a_1+a_11=2a_6.

m-09.title: Test positive. What probability say e defective?
m-09.goal: Change your judgment about probability of defect each time new test result come, and explain why ignoring original defect rate (prior probability) make you overestimate.
m-09.material: 2% of products from factory defective. Tester mark defective product "positive" (meaning defective) with probability 90%, and wrongly mark normal product "positive" with probability 5%. Mark meaning not defective na "negative." Once we know whether product defective or normal, assume repeated test results no affect one another.
m-09.thinking.0: Revise probability judgment as more information come
m-09.thinking.1: Compare intuition and calculation for conditional probability
m-09.thinking.2: Explain effect of base rate (defect rate)
m-09.prereq.1: Meaning of conditional probability (Probability and Statistics level)
m-09.s.s1.prompt: Test results come one after another. Each time, choose how likely product defective.
m-09.s.s1.hint.0: Suppose 1000 products dey, first write how many defective and how many normal.
m-09.s.s1.hint.1: Count defective and normal products wey give result asked about (positive, two positives, etc.).
m-09.s.s1.st.0.ask: About wetin be probability say product defective?
m-09.s.s1.st.0.after: Out of 1000, 20 defective and 980 normal. Out of 20 defective, 90%, that is 18, test positive; out of 980 normal, 5%, that is 49, too test positive. Out of 67 positives, 18 really defective, so about 27%. Normal products far more, so even accurate tester still give low probability.
m-09.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Defect rate na 2%, so e seem low, but positive result make probability rise.
m-09.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Out of 67 positives from 1000, 18 defective, matching your count.
m-09.s.s1.st.0.r.c: 90% mean "chance defective product test positive." "Chance positive product really defective" different. Remember normal products far more.
m-09.s.s1.st.0.r.d: Tester accuracy make am feel high. Suppose 1000 products and count how many positive.
m-09.s.s1.st.1.info: Same product tested one more time, and e positive again.
m-09.s.s1.st.1.ask: Now about how likely say e defective?
m-09.s.s1.st.2.ask: Now about how likely say e defective?
m-09.s.s1.st.1.after: Out of 20 defective, 0.9×0.9=0.81, that is 16.2, test positive twice; out of 980 normal, 0.05×0.05=0.0025, that is 2.45, positive twice. 16.2÷(16.2+2.45)≈0.87, so about 87%. One positive weak, but positives back-to-back raise chance plenty. 1000
m-09.s.s1.st.1.r.a: Normal product fit test positive twice too (0.05×0.05). Check how many.
m-09.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Second positive na new information. If you count only cases positive twice in a row, how share of defective products change?
m-09.s.s1.st.1.r.c: E rise from first 27%, but might rise more. Count by hand only cases positive both times.
m-09.s.s1.st.1.r.d: This match value from counting cases positive both times (about 87%).
m-09.s.s1.st.2.info: Third test result na "negative." (First two positive.)
m-09.s.s1.st.2.after: Out of 20 defective, positive-positive-negative probability na 0.9×0.9×0.1=0.081, that is 1.62; out of 980 normal, positive-positive-negative na 0.05×0.05×0.95=0.002375, that is 2.3275. 1.62÷(1.62+2.3275)≈0.41, so about 41%. New information fit increase or decrease probability.
m-09.s.s1.st.2.r.a: This match value from comparing about 1.62 defective and 2.33 normal products wey give positive-positive-negative (about 41%).
m-09.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Third negative na information wey lower chance say e defective. What probability say defective product test negative?
m-09.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Even though one negative show, the first two positives still count. Wetin happen when we consider all three results?
m-09.s.s1.st.2.r.d: If we look only third negative, e seem like probability gats drop, but two positive results already happen. Count positive-positive-negative cases on defective side and normal side, then compare.
m-09.s.s1.reflect: Across three tests, defect probability change from 27% to 87% to 41%. Which way and why each result move probability? Wetin first guess of 90% miss?
m-09.s.s2.prompt: Explain to friend wey believe "Tester catch 90% of defective products, so if positive, chance defective 90% or more" why e no so.
m-09.s.s2.hint.0: Out of 1000 products, split positive results into defective and normal and count dem.
m-09.s.s2.hint.1: Among positive products, calculate share wey really defective.
m-09.s.s2.placeholder: For example: Defective products from beginning ...
m-09.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Your explanation distinguish "chance defective product test positive" from "chance positive product defective"?
m-09.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You mention number of normal products wey test positive?
m-09.s.s2.model.0: Defective products only 2% from start, so 20 out of 1000. Among 980 normal, 5%, that is 49, too test positive. Out of 67 positives, 18 really defective, so about 27%.
m-09.s.s2.model.1: Even if tester 90% accurate, normal products far more; so normal-but-positive products fit pass truly defective positive ones. One positive no mean 90% chance.
m-09.s.s2.model.2: Defective products rare and most normal, so number wrongly marked positive despite normal fit pass true defective positives. So even with positive result, chance of defect no high.

m-01.title: Looking at claim "Multiplying always make it bigger"
m-01.goal: Learn say few examples no guarantee "always," then make your own counterexamples where product no bigger than starting number, and state when product really bigger.
m-01.material: Minji say, "Multiplication makes things bigger. 3×4=12 bigger than 3, 5×2=10 bigger than 5, 7×6=42 bigger than 7. So any number you multiply by, answer always bigger than starting number!"
m-01.thinking.0: Check overgeneralized conclusion even when plenty examples dey
m-01.prereq.0: Multiplying whole numbers by decimals (Grade 5-6 level, e.g. 8×0.5)
m-01.s.s1.prompt: Which line in Minji argument hard to believe? Choose one.
m-01.s.s1.hint.0: First check whether each of the 3 calculations correct.
m-01.s.s1.hint.1: Write multipliers 4, 2, 6 side by side and see whether dem get anything in common.
m-01.s.s1.line.3: So any number you multiply by, answer always bigger than starting number.
m-01.s.s1.explain: Wetin you see depend on which line you choose. If you choose any of first 3, calculation and comparison correct. Problem no be "Are the examples right?" but "How far you fit go with few examples?" Last line wrong. Minji only look at 3 examples where multipliers 4, 2, 6 all same kind of number, then say "any number, always." Even with plenty examples, if you no test some kind of number, "always" no prove.
m-01.s.s2.prompt: Make 2 examples with different multipliers wey show Minji claim wrong. Starting number must be whole number at least 1, multiplier bigger than 0 (whole or decimal okay), and product no bigger than starting number.
m-01.s.s2.hint.0: Minji only try multipliers 4, 2, 6. Choose kind of number she no try yet and multiply starting number by am.
m-01.s.s2.hint.1: Try changing multiplier different ways, compare product with starting number, and look for cases where product no bigger.
m-01.s.s2.ok.c1: Starting number na whole number at least 1.
m-01.s.s2.fail.c1: Use whole number at least 1 as starting number.
m-01.s.s2.fail.c2: Use multiplier bigger than 0. (0 left out of this activity.)
m-01.s.s2.ok.c3: Product no become bigger than starting number. Minji claim no hold.
m-01.s.s2.fail.c3: Product become bigger. Compare with starting number.
m-01.s.s2.explain: For example, 8×0.5=4 smaller than 8, and 6×1=6 equal 6. Both cases no "get bigger." One counterexample enough to break "always."
m-01.s.s3.prompt: When you multiply starting number (value bigger than 0) by another number, which statement say exactly, with nothing missing, when answer bigger than starting number?
m-01.s.s3.hint.0: Change multiplier different ways and make table of (starting number)×(multiplier).
m-01.s.s3.hint.1: In table, separate rows where answer bigger than starting number from rows where no, then look what different about multipliers.
m-01.s.s3.r.a: If multiplier bigger than 1, answer get bigger; if e be 1, same; if e between 0 and 1, answer smaller. This option state exact boundary.
m-01.s.s3.r.b: Whole numbers include 1. Check 8×1 and you fit correct this statement.
m-01.s.s3.r.c: Some decimals like 1.5 bigger than 1; others like 0.5 smaller. Being decimal alone no decide.
m-01.s.s3.r.d: If bigger than 2, answer definitely bigger, but some numbers below 2, like 1.5 too make am bigger. This no cover every case.
m-01.s.s3.r.e: Even if starting number big, multiplying by 0.5 make am smaller. Multiplier decide whether answer get bigger.
m-01.s.s3.explain: If multiplier bigger than 1, answer bigger; if e equal 1, same; if between 0 and 1, answer smaller. So correct statement no be "always bigger," but "multiplying by a number bigger than 1 makes it bigger."
m-01.s.s4.prompt: Wetin you want tell Minji? Use examples (numbers) wey you just make to explain why she wrong and when answer really get bigger.
m-01.s.s4.hint.0: You fit use numbers from two examples you just made.

m-01.s.s4.selfAssess.1: You know even one example enough to disprove "always"?
m-01.s.s4.selfAssess.2: You too say "which numbers make it bigger when you multiply"?
m-01.s.s4.model.0: No. 8×0.5=4 smaller than 8. E only get bigger than starting number when multiplier bigger than 1.
m-01.s.s4.model.1: E no always bigger. 6×1=6 stay same, and 10×0.1=1 get smaller too. You must multiply by number bigger than 1 to make it bigger.

m-10.title: If f'(a)=0, na extremum?
m-10.goal: Use derivative sign changes as evidence to judge claim "If f'(a)=0, na extremum," make counterexample, and state condition for extremum.
m-10.material:
Jihun say, "For function f, if f'(a)=0, then e get extremum (maximum or minimum) at x=a." He check derivative sign f'(x) for three functions near x=0.
Function | f'(x) | f'(−1) | f'(−0.1) | f'(0) | f'(0.1) | f'(1)
f(x)=x² | 2x | − | − | 0 | + | +
f(x)=x³ | 3x² | + | + | 0 | + | +
f(x)=−x⁴ | −4x³ | + | + | 0 | − | −
(The + and − in table show derivative signs. Read x², x³, and −x⁴ as "x squared," "x cubed," "negative x to the fourth.")
m-10.prereq.1: Derivative sign, increasing/decreasing, meaning of maximum and minimum (Calculus level)
m-10.s.s1.prompt: Look table and choose every function you think get extremum (max or min) at x=0.
m-10.s.s1.hint.0: For each function, compare f' signs on left and right of x=0.
m-10.s.s1.hint.1: Use fact when sign changes, function change from increasing to decreasing (or reverse).
m-10.s.s1.r.a: If you missed x²: f' sign change from − to +. Function goes down then up, so minimum.
m-10.s.s1.r.b: f'(x) sign na + before and after x=0. Function increase, pause at 0, then increase again, so no extremum.
m-10.s.s1.r.c: If you missed −x⁴: f' sign change from + to −. Function go up then down, so maximum.
m-10.s.s1.explain: For x², f' sign change from − to +, so minimum; for −x⁴, + to −, so maximum. For x³, f'(0)=0 but sign no change, so no extremum.
m-10.s.s2.prompt: Which judgment fit best for Jihun claim "If f'(a)=0, then extremum dey at x=a"?
m-10.s.s2.hint.0: If claim say "always," think wetin make am false if one case dey.
m-10.s.s2.hint.1: For each function on table, compare f' signs before and after x=0 where f'(0)=0.
m-10.s.s2.o.a: True. All three functions have f'(0)=0, so dem get extremum.
m-10.s.s2.r.a: All three get f'(0)=0, but only two get extremum. Check every table result.
m-10.s.s2.o.b: False. Even if f'(0)=0, one function on table no get extremum.
m-10.s.s2.r.b: You show with one counterexample say "always" false.
m-10.s.s2.o.c: True. Two of three functions get extremum, so e hold for most.
m-10.s.s2.r.c: A claim saying "always" no become true because e hold for most cases. Find even one case where e fail.
m-10.s.s2.o.d: No fit judge. Only three functions dey, hard to decide.
m-10.s.s2.r.d: Even with few functions, one counterexample enough to judge "always" false. Check if table get counterexample.
m-10.s.s2.explain: f(x)=x³ has f'(0)=0 but no extremum, so e counterexample. Claim "always hold" fail with one counterexample only.
m-10.s.s3.prompt: Make two cubic functions f(x)=ax³+bx²+cx+d with integer coefficients and different a values, where f'(0)=0 but no extremum at x=0.
m-10.s.s3.hint.0: Write f'(x) using a,b,c and find f'(0).
m-10.s.s3.hint.1: Compare why x³ on table no extremum (f' sign) and how e different from x².
m-10.s.s3.ok.c1: E cubic function and coefficients integers.
m-10.s.s3.fail.c1: a must be nonzero integer; b,c,d too must be integers. 0
m-10.s.s3.fail.c2: f'(0) no be 0. Put x=0 inside f'(x)=3ax²+2bx+c.
m-10.s.s3.ok.c3: f'(x)=3ax², so sign no change before and after x=0.
m-10.s.s3.fail.c3: f'(x) sign change before and after x=0, so extremum form. Check sign near zero in f'(x)=x(3ax+2b). 0
m-10.s.s3.explain: f'(x)=3ax²+2bx+c, so f'(0)=c. If c=0, then f'(x)=x(3ax+2b), and if b≠0, sign change near x=0 and extremum form. If b=0, f'(x)=3ax², sign same before and after 0, so no extremum.
m-10.s.s4.prompt: You wan fix Jihun claim properly. For "If f'(a)=0 and _____, then e get extremum at x=a," write condition for blank.
m-10.s.s4.hint.0: For x² and −x⁴ (extrema) and x³ (not), compare how f' sign differ before and after x=0.
m-10.s.s4.hint.1: Write signs side by side left/right of x=0 for x² and x³, then state difference in one sentence.
m-10.s.s4.selfAssess.0: You write it as condition comparing left and right of x=a?
m-10.s.s4.selfAssess.1: Does condition reject x³ case, where f'(x)=0 at x=0 but no extremum?
m-10.s.s4.model.0: f'(x) sign change before and after x=a.
m-10.s.s4.model.1: This case: left of x=a function increase then right change to decrease (or reverse), so increasing/decreasing switch.
m-10.s.s4.model.2: Left and right of x=a, f'(x) change from + to − or from − to +.
m-10.s.s4.model.3: f''(a)≠0. (If second derivative no be 0, e extremum.)
m-10.s.s4.modelNote.3: This na second derivative test. E sufficient condition but no necessary condition.

m-05.s.s1.r.e: Calculate difference yourself between B fees at 0GB and 4GB. If e cost 1500 won for 1GB, how much 4GB cost?

m-05.s.s2.prompt: Three friends say which plan cheaper. Considering table and fee rules, which claim most appropriate?
m-05.s.s2.hint.0: Find where fees of A and B change places in table.
m-05.s.s2.hint.1: Write which one cheaper before and after the change.
m-05.s.s2.o.a: Jisu: A cheaper because fee per 1GB na 1000 won, below B 1500 won.
m-05.s.s2.r.a: Look again at 0, 4, and 8GB in table. Even if unit price lower, what happen at first because of base fee?
m-05.s.s2.o.b: Minho: B cheaper because base fee 3000 won, below A's 9000 won.
m-05.s.s2.r.b: Look again at 16GB and 20GB rows. As usage increase, wetin happen to base-fee difference?
m-05.s.s2.o.c: Hana: E depend on usage. Below 12GB B cheaper; above am, A cheaper.
m-05.s.s2.r.c: This judgment correct for table and fee rules. Base fee and unit price work opposite ways, so dem switch at 12GB.
m-05.s.s2.o.d: Junho: Whichever you choose, na same, because at 12GB fee same, 21000 won.
m-05.s.s2.r.d: For table, 12GB na only usage amount with same fees. Check other rows again.
m-05.s.s2.o.e: Seoa: E depend on usage. Below 8GB B cheaper; above am A cheaper.
m-05.s.s2.r.e: At 8GB, B still cheaper (15000 won and 17000 won). The fees become equal and switch at 12GB, no be 8GB.
m-05.s.s2.explain: B base fee cheaper by 6000 won, while A unit price cheaper by 500 won. Dem meet at 12GB; below that B cheaper, above that A cheaper. If you look at only one usage amount, you fit wrongly generalize like Jisu or Minho.
m-05.s.s3.prompt: Which plan you go recommend to person wey use 10GB each month? 10GB no dey table. Write wetin you use as evidence.

m-05.s.s3.selfAssess.0: For 10GB wey no dey table, wetin you use: calculation from formula, or the fact say e between 8GB and 12GB?
m-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You know say you assume fees dey increase at steady rate?
m-05.s.s3.model.0: For 10GB, A na 9000+1000×10=19000 won and B na 3000+1500×10=18000 won. So B cheaper.
m-05.s.s3.model.1: For 8GB, B cheaper; at 12GB, fees same. 10GB dey between dem, so you fit say B cheaper. But I assume fee increase steadily with amount used.

m-08.title: Find all triangles with perimeter 12
m-08.goal: Discover by testing triangle condition, then explain how you know you find every case meeting the condition.
m-08.material: Some sticks dey. You want choose 3 sticks as triangle sides. All lengths na whole numbers (cm), and perimeter (sum of three lengths) na 12cm. You no cut or join dem together.
m-08.thinking.0: Test hypothesis yourself to discover condition wey make am true
m-08.thinking.2: Explain why you find all cases without missing any
m-08.prereq.1: Basics of inequalities (compare sum of two values with one value)
m-08.s.s1.prompt: Three sticks get lengths 3cm, 3cm, and 6cm. Fit you make triangle? (Sum na 12cm.) Decide by imagining how you go lay dem down yourself.
m-08.s.s1.hint.0: Put longest stick, 6cm, on ground, and stand other two at both ends so dem touch.
m-08.s.s1.hint.1: Add lengths of other two sticks and compare with longest one.
m-08.s.s1.r.a: 3+3+6=12, so perimeter correct. But correct perimeter different from sides closing into triangle. Wetin happen when you put two sticks against 6cm stick?
m-08.s.s1.r.b: Good judgment. Even if you join two 3cm sticks over 6cm one, combined length same, so no top corner go form.
m-08.s.s1.o.c: You no fit know until you draw am yourself.
m-08.s.s1.r.c: You fit compare stick lengths without draw. Which lengths you gats compare?
m-08.s.s1.explain: Even if you join two 3cm sticks, length na 6cm, same as 6cm stick. Two sticks lie flat on the 6cm stick, no corner form, so triangle no form.
m-08.s.s2.prompt: Find and enter every different triangle with perimeter 12cm where all side lengths whole numbers. (Triangles with sides in different order count as same.)
m-08.s.s2.hint.0: First choose longest side length, then find matching sum of the other two sides.
m-08.s.s2.hint.1: Check whether the three sides you make form triangle by comparing longest with sum of other two.
m-08.s.s2.ok.c1: All three side lengths na whole numbers.
m-08.s.s2.fail.c1: Use whole numbers 1 or more for side lengths.
m-08.s.s2.fail.c2: The three sides no add up to 12.
m-08.s.s2.fail.c3: Triangle no form. Compare longest side with sum of other two.
m-08.s.s2.explain: Only triangles wey fit conditions na (2,5,5), (3,4,5), and (4,4,4). If longest side equal or longer than sum of other sides, like (3,3,6) or (1,5,6), no triangle form. 1 2 3 3 3 4 4 4 5 5
m-08.s.s3.prompt: How you sure say "na all, no more"? Explain the method you use to find all without missing any.
m-08.s.s3.hint.0: First find biggest and smallest lengths longest side fit get.
m-08.s.s3.hint.1: Once longest side set, write sum of other two and check each possible pair one by one.
m-08.s.s3.placeholder: For example, if the longest side na ...
m-08.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You clearly write criterion (like longest side) you use to split into cases?
m-08.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You check with numbers which ones possible and impossible for each case?
m-08.s.s3.model.0: Longest side gats less than 6, so e fit be 5 or less, and at least 12÷3=4. If longest side na 4, only 4,4,4. If 5, other two sum na 7, so two ways: (2,5) and (3,4). Three total.
m-08.s.s3.model.1: I check in order from shortest side 1 to 4. If 1, other two sum 11, and all pairs like 5,6 no make triangle; if 2, 5,5; if 3,4,5; if 4,4,4. Checking one by one, nothing miss. 3 4.5
m-08.s.s3.model.2: I set one side and split remaining sum. If longest na 5, other two sum 7, so (2,5) and (3,4); if longest 4, only (4,4). I check every case like this, so 3 total.
